case: MySQL and MariaDB ENUM and SET parser/keyed edits across twelve SQL modes
contract: Grid parsing validates values against declared ENUM/SET members, including apostrophe and backslash metadata, and refuses unknown labels or members.

Bound keyed edits preserve ENUM label bytes and multi-member SET masks under twelve modes: default; NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; ANSI_QUOTES with and without NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; and STRICT_TRANS_TABLES or STRICT_ALL_TABLES, each alone and with ANSI_QUOTES, NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, or both.
Blank input retains shared SQL NULL/required-field behavior, while explicit empty input selects an empty ENUM label or empty SET value; native ordinals/masks distinguish empty values from NULL.
The permissive-mode control demonstrates that an unknown ENUM label can coerce to the error value and an unknown SET member can be dropped; control updates roll back.
Untouched sibling rows retain native ordinals, masks and label bytes in every mode.
The literal label NULL remains distinct from SQL NULL on both engines.
MariaDB reports declared ENUM/SET members; valid apostrophe/backslash values preserve native ordinals, masks and bytes, while invalid values are refused.
